title_en: Working hours, rest, leave and holidays in Lebanon
title_ar: ساعات العمل والراحة والإجازات والعطل في لبنان
question_en: How many hours can an employee be made to work in Lebanon, and what rest, annual leave, sick leave, maternity leave and public holidays does the law give?
question_ar: كم ساعة يجوز تشغيل الأجير في لبنان، وما هي الراحة والإجازة السنوية والمرضية والأمومة والعطل الرسمية التي يقرها القانون؟
sub_questions: What is the maximum working week and how is overtime paid?
How long must the daily break and the weekly rest be?
How many days of annual leave does an employee get?
How much paid and half-paid sick leave is there by length of service?
How long is maternity leave and who pays during it?
Which public holidays are days off, and what if the holiday falls on a Sunday?
notes: Labour Code art 31 sets the 48-hour week (not agricultural). Overtime pay: art 33 (50% more) applies to emergency cases up to 12 hours a day; the Code has no general overtime rate for ordinary work, so say so rather than invent one. Art 12-3 (added by the recent amendment on part-time work) gives 50% extra for overtime of part-time workers. Arts 12-1 to 12-8 cover compressed working weeks, part-time, seasonal and remote work. Annual leave: art 39 gives 15 days paid after one year in the establishment (the text is the original; the database has no amendment to 21 days). Sick leave: art 40 scale by service, art 41 allows employer to cut annual leave to 8 days if sick leave exceeds a month, art 42 bars dismissal during sick leave. Maternity: art 28 (ten weeks, as amended) and art 29 (full pay, no dismissal); the Social Security Law art 26 pays the maternity allowance to insured women for the ten weeks and art 23 pays sickness allowance (50% then 75% of daily earnings, from day 4). Public holidays: the Labour Code has no list; Decree 15215/2005 art 1 lists the holidays for public administrations and municipalities, and only says that private-sector establishments close the day after Labour Day if it falls on a Sunday; do not claim it binds private employers for other holidays (art 4 says a holiday on a Sunday is not replaced). Art 43 makes agreements below these minimums void.

pack.why: Labour Code: working week, flexible/part-time work, overtime, breaks, weekly rest, bereavement and annual leave, sick leave, maternity leave, nullity of worse terms
Social Security Law: sickness allowance and maternity allowance paid by the Fund
Decree 15215/2005: official holidays (public administrations, with the Labour Day rule for private establishments)
